code: radius_threshold <- 250000  unknowns <- organism_raw |> filter(scientificName == "Arachnocampa") references <- organism_raw |> filter(scientificName == "Arachnocampa flava")  assign_if_close_to_flava <- function(lat, lon, flava_data, radius) {   dists <- distHaversine(     matrix(c(lon, lat), ncol = 2),     matrix(c(flava_data$obs_lon, flava_data$obs_lat), ncol = 2)   )   if (any(dists <= radius)) "Arachnocampa flava" else "Arachnocampa" }  unknowns_updated <- unknowns |>    rowwise() |>    mutate(scientificName = assign_if_close_to_flava(obs_lat, obs_lon, references, radius_threshold)) |>    ungroup()  organism <- organism_raw |>    filter(scientificName != "Arachnocampa") |>    bind_rows(unknowns_updated) |>    filter(!is.na(obs_lat), !is.na(obs_lon), !is.na(month),          scientificName %in% c("Arachnocampa flava", "Arachnocampa tasmaniensis"))  mysave(organism_name, organism)

title: Orchids
code: organism <- obs_data(taxa, start, end, your_email=email) |> polished_data() orchids_subset <- read_csv("../data-raw/orchids_subset.csv") organism <- organism %>%   mutate(     genus   = word(scientificName, 1),     epithet = word(scientificName, 2),     # species-level if it has two words and the 2nd isn't a vague token     is_species = !is.na(epithet) &       !str_detect(epithet, "^(sp|spp|cf|aff|x|×)\\.?$"),     binomial = if_else(is_species, paste(genus, epithet), NA_character_)   )  organism <- organism |>   filter(is_species==TRUE,           scientificName %in% orchids_subset$scientificName,          obs_state == "Western Australia") |>    select(1:13)

what: Step 1: Identify Top 3 Weather Stations per Organism
title: Weather Data
code: organism_names <- c("orchids", "gouldian_finch", "manta_rays", "glowworms") load("../data/weather_stations.rda") all_top_stations <- list()  for (org in organism_names) {   load(paste0("../data/", org, ".rda"))   org_data <- get(org)    top_stations <- org_data %>%     count(ws_id, sort = TRUE) %>%     slice_max(n, n = 3) %>%     left_join(weather_stations, by = c("ws_id")) %>%     mutate(organism = org) %>%     select(organism, ws_id)    all_top_stations[[org]] <- top_stations }  top_stations <- bind_rows(all_top_stations) save(top_stations, file = "../data/top_stations.rda")

title: Weather Data
code: load("../data/weather_stations.rda") load("../data/top_stations.rda") df <- left_join(top_stations, weather_stations, by = "ws_id") df

title: Weather Data
code: aus_map <- ne_states(country = "Australia", returnclass = "sf") ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = aus_map, fill = "gray95", color = "gray50") +   geom_point(data = df, aes(x = stn_lon, y = stn_lat, color = organism), shape = 2, alpha = 0.8, size = 3) +   coord_sf(xlim = c(110, 155), ylim = c(-45, -10)) +   theme_minimal()

what: Optional: Download Weather Data from GSOD
title: Weather Data
code: # Download and prepare data (optional) weather_data_list <- lapply(top_stations$ws_id, function(stn) {   get_GSOD(years = 2014:2024, station = stn) })  top_weather <- bind_rows(weather_data_list) |>    transmute(     ws_id = STNID,     stn_lat = LATITUDE,     stn_lon = LONGITUDE,     date = YEARMODA,     year = YEAR,     month = MONTH,     day = DAY,     weekday = lubridate::wday(date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE,                                week_start = getOption("lubridate.week.start", 1)),     dayofyear = YDAY,     temp = TEMP,     min = MIN,     max = MAX,     dewp = DEWP,     rh = RH,     prcp = PRCP,     rainy = ifelse(PRCP > 5, 1, 0),     wind_speed = WDSP,     max_speed = MXSPD   )  # Save to data folder assign("weather_data", top_weather) save(weather_data, file = "../data/weather_data.rda")

title: Australia Weather Station
text: vignette demonstrates download, process, visualize locations weather stations across Australia using GSODR package. stations key understanding long-term climate patterns ecotourism studies.

what: Step 1: Download and Clean Weather Station Data
title: Australia Weather Station
code: # Download and filter weather stations for Australia stations_all <- get_inventory()  weather_stations <- stations_all |>   filter(CTRY == "AS") |>   select(STNID, NAME, LAT, LON) |>    rename(stn_lat = LAT, stn_lon = LON, ws_id = STNID, stname = NAME) |>    distinct(stn_lat, stn_lon, .keep_all = TRUE) |>    filter(stn_lat >= -44, stn_lat <= -8, stn_lon >= 110, stn_lon <= 160) |>    reverse_geocode(lat = stn_lat, long = stn_lon, method = "osm")

what: Step 2: Extract State Information from Addresses
title: Australia Weather Station
code: weather_stations <- weather_stations %>%   rowwise() %>%   mutate(parsed = list(parse_address(address))) %>%   unnest(parsed) %>%   ungroup()
